question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{7}(x+\sqrt{y}), & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{4}{7},$ find $\text{E}[2X+Y].$
question.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[X].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[Y].$

The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{6}{7}(x+\sqrt{y})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6}{7}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+x\sqrt{y}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{6}{7}(\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{y}) \\  & =\frac{3}{7}(2\sqrt{y}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{3}{7}(2\sqrt{y}+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{7}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{y}^{3/2}+y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{7}{[\frac{4}{5}{y}^{5/2}+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{7}(\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{39}{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X+Y] & =2\,\text{E}[X]+\text{E}[Y] \\  & =2(\frac{4}{7})+(\frac{39}{70}) \\  & =\frac{80+39}{70} \\  & =\frac{17}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
